issues.t: CVT automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Shuddering or jerking when pulling away, a whining noise, slipping, a flashing transmission warning, or the car going into a weak limp mode or refusing to move.
issues.why: The base Cooper of this generation used a continuously variable automatic (CVT) that is a well-known weak point. Internal wear eventually makes it slip or fail completely.
issues.next: Get it scanned and checked by a shop that knows MINIs as soon as symptoms start. Repairs usually mean a rebuilt or used transmission, so get a quote before deciding whether the car is worth fixing.

issues.t: Early 5-speed manual gearbox failure
issues.sym: Growling or whining from the gearbox that changes with speed, grinding or popping out of gear, and eventually a gearbox that stops working.
issues.why: Early base Coopers used a 5-speed manual (the Midlands unit) with known reliability problems. MINI switched to a stronger Getrag gearbox for 2005.
issues.next: Have the gearbox and its oil checked if it is noisy. Many owners replace a failing early unit with the later, stronger gearbox.

issues.t: Power steering pump overheating or failing
issues.sym: Steering suddenly turns heavy, especially at parking speeds, sometimes with a steering warning. It may come and go at first, often after a long drive on a hot day.
issues.why: These cars use an electric motor to run the hydraulic power steering pump. It sits low at the front, and its small cooling fan can be damaged by debris or fail, so the pump overheats and quits.
issues.next: Steer carefully and have the pump, its fan and the fluid checked. Check for open recalls too, since MINI recalled 2002-2005 cars for loss of steering assist.

issues.t: Loss of power steering assist (recall)
issues.sym: Steering becomes very heavy at low speed or when parking, and a power steering warning may light up.
issues.why: MINI found the electro-hydraulic power steering system on these years can lose assist temporarily or for good, which makes the car harder to steer.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-660 and have a MINI dealer do the free inspection and repair.

issues.t: Cracked coolant expansion tank
issues.sym: Coolant drips or a sweet smell under the hood, a low-coolant warning, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The plastic coolant overflow tank on the Cooper S cracks after years of heating and cooling. MINI later revised the tank, but older tanks still fail.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and look for cracks or crusty residue on the tank. Do not keep driving if the engine is overheating.

issues.t: Oil leaks from crank sensor seal and front main seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the car, oily residue on the lower engine, or a burning-oil smell.
issues.why: The rubber O-ring under the crankshaft sensor and the front crankshaft seal harden with age and start to leak.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the oil level and have the leak traced. The seals are simple parts, but the front main seal is a bigger job.

issues.t: Clutch wearing out early
issues.sym: The clutch slips (engine revs rise but the car doesn't speed up), the pedal feels different, it is hard to get into gear, or you smell a burning odor.
issues.why: RepairPal lists early clutch wear as a common complaint on manual MINI Coopers. City driving and a heavier dual-mass flywheel on some models add wear.
issues.next: Have the clutch checked once it starts slipping; it only gets worse. Ask whether the flywheel needs replacing at the same time.

issues.t: Passenger airbag turned off by faulty seat sensor (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag "off" light shows with an adult in the seat, or the airbag warning light is on.
issues.why: The occupant detection mat in the passenger seat can fail, so the system wrongly switches the passenger airbag off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-205. A dealer replaces the seat mat free.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A loud rattle, like a diesel, for a few seconds after a cold start. It can get louder and last longer over time, and a check engine light may come on.
issues.why: A weak timing chain tensioner lets the chain go slack and slap against its plastic guides, and the chain stretches. If ignored the chain can jump a tooth and badly damage the engine.
issues.next: Do not ignore the rattle. Keep the oil full and changed often, and have a MINI specialist fit the latest tensioner; if it still rattles the chain and guides need replacing.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Intermittent loss of power, stuttering under acceleration, long cranking or hard starting, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The turbo engine uses a high-pressure pump for its direct fuel injection. These pumps are a known failure item on Cooper S and John Cooper Works models.
issues.next: Have the fuel pressure codes read. If the pump is failing, replace it before it leaves you stranded, and ask a dealer about any extended coverage for your car.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, misfires and loss of power, sometimes with a check engine light. It can show up as early as 20,000-30,000 miles.
issues.why: On direct-injection engines, fuel no longer washes over the intake valves, so oily vapor from the crankcase bakes on as carbon and blocks airflow.
issues.next: Have misfire codes diagnosed first. If carbon is the cause, a walnut-shell blasting cleaning restores performance; some owners add an oil catch can to slow it down.

issues.t: Turbo oil feed line leak and turbo failure
issues.sym: Oil leaking around the turbo, blue smoke, a whistling or grinding noise, or loss of boost and power.
issues.why: The pipe that carries oil to the turbo leaks at its joints and can clog with baked oil on high-mileage cars, starving the turbo of oil until it fails.
issues.next: Have leaks around the turbo checked. Replacing the feed pipe early can prevent turbo damage. Change oil on time.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil seep
issues.sym: Oil seeping around the edges of the valve cover or in the spark plug area, and a burning-oil smell after driving.
issues.why: The rocker (valve) cover gasket on the turbo engine hardens and lets oil weep out.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed. It is not urgent if small, but oil dripping on hot parts can smoke, and oil in the plug wells can cause misfires.

issues.t: Oil filter housing gasket leak
issues.sym: Oil dripping under the car, oil on the belt or the front of the engine, and a burning-oil smell.
issues.why: The gasket between the oil filter housing and the engine block hardens and leaks. Oil can soak the drive belt and cause it to slip or break.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and fixed soon, before oil damages the belt or nearby hoses.

issues.t: Water pump and thermostat housing coolant leaks
issues.sym: Coolant drips, a sweet smell, a low-coolant warning, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: The water pump and plastic thermostat housing on these engines are known to leak as they age.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant only when cold and have the leak traced. Stop driving if the temperature warning comes on.

issues.t: Turbo coolant pump fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, sometimes with coolant or overheating warnings.
issues.why: The electric auxiliary water pump that cools the turbo after shutdown has a circuit board that can overheat and smolder, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 12V-008 and 18V-248. A dealer replaces the pump free. If you smell burning, park outside and away from buildings until it is fixed.

issues.t: Footwell module water damage fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: A wet driver-side footwell carpet, lights or windows acting strangely, or a burning smell inside the car.
issues.why: Water and road salt can reach the footwell control module under the driver's side, corrode it and cause a short circuit that could start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-337 (it applies in salt-belt states). A dealer does the repair free. Fix any water leak into the cabin too.

issues.t: Cracked oil filter housing (2.0L turbo)
issues.sym: Oil or coolant leaking under the car, often between 50,000 and 100,000 miles, and sometimes a low-coolant warning.
issues.why: The oil filter housing on BMW's B48 2.0L turbo engine, used in the Cooper S and JCW, can crack. It also carries coolant, so it can leak both fluids.
issues.next: Have any oil or coolant leak diagnosed soon. The housing sits under the intake manifold, so the repair is labor-heavy; get a quote from an independent BMW/MINI shop as well as the dealer.

issues.t: Electric water pump or coolant hose failure (2.0L turbo)
issues.sym: Coolant puddles under the car, a coolant warning, the engine overheating, or the car going into reduced power.
issues.why: The electric water pump and plastic coolant return hoses on the B48 2.0L turbo engine are known to fail and leak.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. Have the cooling system pressure-tested, and check hoses and the pump before buying a used car with this engine.

issues.t: Car can roll away when leaving it out of Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car may not warn you or hold itself when you get out without putting it in Park.
issues.why: Transmission software loaded by dealers could let the driver leave the car while it was not in Park, so it might roll away.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for recall 14V-789; a dealer reprograms the transmission control module free.

issues.t: Passenger front airbag may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: There is no warning sign; the recall notice is the only way to know.
issues.why: A manufacturing error could stop the passenger front airbag from deploying correctly in some low-speed crashes.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-628. A dealer replaces the airbag module free.

issues.t: Rear seat side-impact padding missing (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms; the car simply offers less protection to rear passengers in a side crash.
issues.why: Rear seat side-impact protection fell short of the federal safety standard, so extra energy-absorbing material is needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-450 and have the free padding installed.

issues.t: Driver seat belt may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the belt may not lock up as it should in hard braking or a crash.
issues.why: The driver's seat belt emergency locking retractor may not work as designed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-747. A dealer replaces the seat belt assembly free.

issues.t: Engine stalling from crankshaft sensor (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can stall while driving, and may then need restarting.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor had incorrect software and could misread engine position, shutting the engine off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-465. A dealer replaces the sensor free.

issues.t: Rear side trim missing crash pads (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms; side-crash protection is lower than designed.
issues.why: Rear side trim panels were installed without their crash pads, failing a side-impact standard.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-634. A dealer installs the pads free.

issues.t: Head airbags may not fire in a rollover (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; an airbag light may come on in some cases.
issues.why: A faulty rollover sensor in the airbag control unit could stop the head airbags and belt pretensioners from firing in a rollover.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-283. A dealer replaces the control unit free.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt locking feature may release early (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; this matters most when a child seat is installed with the belt.
issues.why: The passenger belt's automatic locking mode, used to hold child seats, may switch off before the belt fully retracts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-554. A dealer inspects and replaces the retractor if needed.

issues.t: Cooper SE high-voltage battery fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: A high-voltage system warning message, or no warning at all.
issues.why: Faults inside the high-voltage battery of the electric Cooper SE can cause a short circuit and a fire risk. MINI recalled about 12,500 US cars in 2024.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-612 and follow MINI's parking and charging instructions until the free repair is done.

issues.t: Cooper SE battery housing can let in water (recall)
issues.sym: A battery or drive-system warning and possible loss of drive power.
issues.why: The high-voltage battery housing may not be fully sealed, so water can get in, which can cause the car to lose power or create a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-302 and get the free dealer repair. Avoid deep water until it is done.

issues.t: Integrated brake system may lose power assist (recall)
issues.sym: Brake or stability control warning lights, a hard brake pedal and longer stopping distances; ABS and stability control may stop working.
issues.why: The integrated brake control unit can malfunction. MINI has issued more than one recall (24V-104 and 26V-422) for this part.
issues.next: If the brake warning lights come on, drive gently to a dealer. Check your VIN for both recalls; the repair is free.

issues.t: Brake control module motor welds can break (recall)
issues.sym: Brake warning lights, a harder pedal and longer stops, with possible loss of rear brakes, ABS and stability control.
issues.why: Welds inside the servomotor of the integrated brake control module may break.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-697. A dealer replaces the brake unit free.

issues.t: Front seat belt retractors may be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the belts may not hold you properly in a crash.
issues.why: A torsion bar inside the front seat belt retractors may have been damaged during production.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-616. A dealer replaces both front retractors free.
